solver.kind: blind AI solver (separate agent, answer-free packet, rubric v2)

S013-01.notes: 'leaving reporters unsure whether she supported it' defines equivocal; candid/vehement contradict, belated irrelevant. Vocabulary word itself is the only hurdle.

S013-02.notes: Text 2 raises self-selection bias, so she would doubt generalizability to non-volunteer firms. B contradicts data; C overgeneralizes; D unsupported.

flags: minor: C is the longest choice and the only one with two contrasting clauses, mirroring the claim's two parts - a mild tell
S013-03.notes: Only C shows both stern manner (scowled) and concealed generosity (secretly left bread). B stern only; D open generosity.

S013-04.notes: 'the one' needs an essential (restrictive) clause to identify which of the two portraits, so no commas: 'the one that hangs in the east wing was...'. B leaves an unpaired comma before the verb; C comma splits subject and verb; D comma before 'that'.

S013-05.notes: Compound predicate (tested ... and replaced) with one subject takes no comma. A is the common trap; B semicolon needs independent clause; C comma splice.

S013-06.notes: Second sentence offers a counterpoint to critics' complaint; 'Then again' signals that contrast. Others signal similarity, causation, restatement.

S013-07.notes: Bakery shuttered, square paved, village 'larger, emptier'; fountain is the only familiar thing. A and C contradicted; D unsupported.

flags: minor: C's parenthetical, compressed phrasing differs stylistically from the other choices and is the only one making a comparison, which is a mild tell
S013-08.notes: Claim is comparative (more pp than any other mode); C gives cycling +8 and notes walking, the only other grower, +3. A (doubled) is the trap - relative not pp comparison; B is a decline; D only walking. Car falls 8 pp, so a 'grew' comparison is unaffected.

S013-09.notes: Heating before grinding implies multistep processing. B contradicts 'long before oats were domesticated'; C overreaches; D contradicts starch evidence.

S013-10.notes: Two competing views, then a study that partly supports each (repetition for nouns, context for verbs).
